correctness.rationale: A tight-alike pair preserves equality and adjacency and sends opposite C4 pairs to distance-two pairs in Cn. The equal/adjacent/opposite cases of the two unmoved values exhaust C4 and each has a response for every n>=5. Structural induction gives existential transfer C4->Cn, hence generalized universal transfer Cn->C4; the explicit sentence eta proves strictness.
residual_risks: The finite replay is bounded; it does not establish the infinite claim. The symbolic extension proof supplies the uniform step.

broader_coverage.reasoning: An existential assertion of stronger preservation counterexamples does not specify C4 and every Cn. The general one-sided game theorem supplies a test, not a winning strategy for these particular cycle structures. Its positive fragment does not itself preserve negated adjacency; one must additionally preserve nonedges and equality (or expand the signature accordingly). The supplied strategy does so, but is not supplied by the cited general characterization. Full back-and-forth equivalence is a different, stronger conclusion and is not claimed here.

value.rationale: Cycle graphs form a natural family of finite relational structures in finite-variable model theory. The exact n=5 comparison is an ingredient of a published preservation example. Determining which part persists for every larger cycle clarifies that example’s mechanism and gives a reusable one-sided three-variable comparison. The distance-two invariant treats the whole family and arbitrary formula depth. This is a structural lemma with an exact strict conclusion, not an arbitrary numerical slice or a claim to improve the stronger preservation-failure theorems.
residual_risks: The contribution is modest and the proof short. No new general preservation theorem or classification among longer cycles is claimed.
